name: IARU Region 1 (Europe, Africa, Middle East)
source: IARU Region 1 HF Band Plan, effective 16 October 2020. 6 m from the IARU Region 1 VHF Handbook v7.51. iaru-r1.org. 2 m, 70 cm and 23 cm: IARU Region 1 VHF Handbook version 10.03 (February 2026), with VHF+ Newsletter 98 (15 October 2026) for the Vienna 2026 changes, iaru-r1.org; FT8, FT4 and MSK144 dial frequencies from the WSJT-X default frequency table (github.com/WSJTX/wsjtx). Receiver bands (not amateur): summarised from the ITU Radio Regulations Article 5 table of allocations and general knowledge of national use. Broad, and not specific to a licence.
note: A regional plan for any country in Region 1 without its own file here. National allocations differ, above all on 160 m, 60 m, 6 m and 4 m: copy this file and edit it for your country. 4 m has no harmonised plan, so it's shown as one block. On VHF and UHF: This is the Handbook 10.03 plan, the edition Newsletter 98 still lists as current. The Vienna conference (September 2026) adopted a supplemental 23 cm plan for countries that have implemented ECC Decision (25)01, with a preferred moonbounce segment at 1299.000-1299.650 MHz from 1 January 2027: check your national rules. It also removed the 144.500-144.794 MHz bandwidth limit and added 434.500 MHz for high-altitude balloon telemetry. 430-432 MHz is planned nationally. National allocations differ: check your own licence and society's plan. The non-amateur bands are only offered on a receiver, and a guide to what's where, not a statement of who may use it.
